name: EvoMem
org: Anonymous organization (Moscow) x Applied AI Institute x Lomonosov Moscow State University
desc: Persistent cross-run memory turns successful evolutionary mutations into provenance-linked advice; on two selected A100 KernelBench targets, the reported combined speedup rises from 2.4941x to 2.7049x versus the same GigaEvo search without memory.
note: The kernel study has only two target tasks, while memory generation uses five separate tasks; pairwise gain averages 16.89% but ranges from 0% to 65.93%, so this is evidence of variable reuse rather than broad KernelBench superiority. No code or winning kernels are linked, and the primary affiliation is anonymized in the paper.
evaluated_on: KernelBench L1 problem 66 and L3 problem 21 on A100 80GB
claim_baseline: the same GigaEvo/Map-Elites search without retrieved EvoMem advice

name: KernelBrain
desc: Multi-fidelity candidate screening promotes only promising variants to expensive measurements, then uses LLM mutation and NCU diagnosis; on six selected A100 kernels it saves 17%-48% wall time on five tasks while matching or improving the compared agent.
note: The study covers only six kernels and 18 shapes, gives no overall geomean, and several best results remain slower than PyTorch. Base kernels come from two different prior agents and comparison budgets are not uniform. arXiv's official history unusually records v1 on 2026-05-19 despite the 2608 identifier; this catalog follows that timestamp.
claim_baseline: PyTorch, the supplied LLM-generated base, and PyTorch KernelAgent, depending on analysis

name: LLM4LLM
desc: Deployment-aware closed loop that profiles real prefill/decode workloads, optimizes and patches kernels, then revalidates the model; across ten language-model workloads it reports 3.91x/6.98x end-to-end geomean on A100/H100, while KernelBench L2 reaches 2.745x/2.628x.
note: All headline speedups are against PyTorch eager, not FlashAttention or another expert kernel. The MIT repo ships the framework and benchmark scripts but explicitly omits generated results and model weights.
claim_baseline: PyTorch eager; torch.compile and selected expert libraries are reported separately

name: Compiler-Grounded Hierarchical Diagnosis
desc: Stateful optimization loop that escalates from pattern triage and profiling to Triton IR and compiler-source diagnosis; on 37 successfully converted Ascend 950 operators it reports 4.35x geomean from the validated initial Triton kernels and, in a separate comparison, 2.60x over Torch NPU.
note: The implementation is integrated into the public CANNBot Skills suite, but the 37 winning kernels are not released. The set excludes failed AI conversions; deep IR/compiler evidence was exercised, yet none of the selected best rounds was directly attributed to those deepest levels.
claim_baseline: validated initial Triton kernel; Torch NPU is a separate post-optimization comparison

name: KDA-Pilot
desc: Evidence-first autonomous SGLang kernel-optimization campaigns with production baselines, strict correctness gates, NCU/KernelWiki evidence, and replayable logs; B200 diffusion tasks include 2.7499x on fuse_scale_shift and 2.3118x on group_norm_silu.
note: Results use fixed multi-shape workloads and a matching local baseline per task; the repository reports no single aggregate score.
claim_baseline: corresponding copied SGLang/Triton/CuTe-DSL production baseline, per task

name: DRTriton
desc: Scalable RL (CSP-DAG synthetic data + curriculum RL + test-time search); DRTriton-7B speeds up 92% of KernelBench L2 vs 23% for GPT-5.2.

name: Kernel-Smith
desc: Evolutionary kernel optimization; upstream contributions to SGLang/LMDeploy.

name: PyTorch KernelAgent
desc: 5-agent system (Profiler / Judge / Analyze / Orchestrator / Benchmark) + NCU + roofline. H100 89% of roofline, 1.56x over torch.compile.

name: AKO / AKO4ALL
desc: Generic coding-agent harness for kernel optimization; 10/13 kernels beat the NVIDIA baseline on SOL-ExecBench.

name: Dr. Kernel
desc: 14B model trained in the KernelGYM RL environment; matches Claude 4.5 Sonnet on KernelBench.

name: GEAK-Triton v2
desc: Extension of the GEAK family for AMD GPUs.

name: Xe-Forge
desc: Multi-stage LLM agent pipeline optimizing Triton kernels on Intel XPU.

name: AKG-AGENT
desc: Multi-agent (Designer / Coder / Verifier / Conductor) builds a DSL-agnostic 'Unified Sketch' then lowers to 5 backends across NVIDIA GPU + Ascend NPU + CPU; 100% on KernelBench L1 (Triton-CUDA pass@4); 1.46x geomean over PyTorch eager on Triton-Ascend.

name: TritonForge
desc: SFT + RL for PyTorch-to-Triton conversion; NVIDIA + AMD cross-platform.

name: TritorX
desc: Generates functionally-correct Triton ATen kernels at scale for emerging accelerators; 481 ATen operators passing 20,000+ PyTorch OpInfo tests.
note: Targets MTIA.

name: KernelFalcon
desc: Predecessor of PyTorch KernelAgent; 100% correctness on all 250 KernelBench L1/L2/L3 tasks.

name: KernelBand
desc: Hierarchical multi-armed bandit for hardware-aware optimization.

name: PRAGMA
desc: Profiling-reasoned multi-agent framework.

name: TritonRL
desc: Trains LLMs to write Triton without 'cheating' (reward-hacking sanitization).

name: ConCuR
desc: Conciseness-driven SFT for kernel generation.

name: KernelGen (Flagos)
desc: Interactive kernel generation platform.

name: SwizzlePerf
desc: Hardware-aware LLM for GPU kernel performance optimization.

name: GEAK
desc: 4-module agent (generator / reflector / evaluator / optimizer); 2.59x speedup on MI300X.
note: The only system decomposing sequential@k vs parallel@k budget.

name: AutoTriton
desc: 8B model trained via SFT + GRPO on 14.1K torch-triton pairs.

name: KernelLLM
desc: Llama 3.1 8B fine-tuned on KernelBook (~25K torch-triton pairs); beats GPT-4o on KernelBench-Triton L1.

name: AKO4X
desc: More advanced/extensible sibling of AKO/AKO4ALL: closed-loop, campaign-based multi-agent system with per-run isolated template workspaces and cross-run per-operator memory archive; agent can propose harness changes gated by a master. Beats FlashInfer expert by up to 30.71x on MLSys 2026 contest DSA sparse attention kernels, ahead of the concurrent Kernel Design Agents (KDA) submission on all five tracks; GEMM result honestly reported as 1.00x (cuBLAS unbeaten).
note: AKO4ALL is a single drop-in Claude Code skill for one workspace with no cross-run memory; AKO4X spawns isolated per-run workspaces and accumulates memory across rounds. 6 target languages: Python/PyTorch, Triton, CUDA, C++, TileLang, CuTe DSL.
claim_baseline: FlashInfer expert kernels; also compared against concurrent Kernel Design Agents (KDA) submission

name: MoziFlux
desc: Apache-2.0 Hermes-driven Triton-Ascend optimizer with CANN/cannsim local and remote gates, an episode store, a 100-task KernelBench L1 corpus, and checked-in optimized kernels with per-task reports.
note: The repository publishes task-level artifacts but no aggregate speedup or pass-rate headline.

name: MoE-Kernel-Agent
desc: Claude-Code-driven Learn->Implement->Optimize harness for Triton MoE kernels; 2nd place Full-Agent/MoE Track, MLSys 2026 FlashInfer Contest, 25.7x median speedup vs PyTorch.
note: Adapted from AKO4ALL's agentic kernel optimization loop; anti-cheat gate blocks delegation to PyTorch APIs, no-op kernels, timing patches, stream injection, uninitialized buffers; benchmarked remotely on NVIDIA B200 via Modal; no license file in repo.
evaluated_on: MLSys 2026 FlashInfer AI Kernel Generation Contest - MoE Track

name: ForgeStencil
desc: Two-agent stencil workflow in which a Kernel Agent profiles and optimizes operators and an App Agent integrates and validates them in real programs; the release reports 1.41x median and 2.05x geomean end-to-end over 100 A100-validated applications.
note: The Apache-2.0 repo ships agents, kernels, provenance/fetch/patch packages, harnesses and a result registry. Large gains can include launch, fusion and host-side restructuring rather than universally faster isolated kernels; H100/B200 coverage is operator-level, and token/iteration/intervention accounting remains a roadmap item.
evaluated_on: 6 stencil families / 32 shape cases on A100
claim_baseline: each application's production GPU path end to end; strongest applicable same-precision public baseline per operator

name: PTXBench / MiniPTXAgent
org: Stanford x Carnegie Mellon University x RadixArk
desc: Auditable benchmark and adaptation pipeline for architecture-specific inline PTX in CUDA and Triton; PTXBench checks correctness, target-instruction execution, sanitizers, SASS and speed against frontier GEMM/attention libraries on H100 and B200.
note: No evaluated model consistently matches frontier libraries across the full suite. The repo publishes the benchmark, FIBServe evaluator and AccRL traces; some supervised data/adapters require access approval, and the reported transfer benefit is uneven across tasks.
claim_baseline: cuBLAS 13.1, cuDNN 9.20 and FlashInfer 0.6.14, depending on task

name: HIERA
desc: Hierarchical workload planner that searches PyTorch compositions, CUDA libraries and custom CUDA, then refines with profiling and expert knowledge; on all 250 KernelBench tasks, Fast_0/Fast_1 are 92.4%/60.4% under its reported 18-candidate setting.
note: The winning implementation may be a PyTorch composite or library call rather than a custom kernel. Results use A100 FP32 and 18 candidates (three rounds by six); no code, prompts or run artifacts are linked.
claim_baseline: PyTorch reference (KernelBench Fast_0/Fast_1); cuDNN for the stencil case study

name: KernelArc
desc: Parallel strategy-specialized agents coordinate through conclusions-only memory and a deterministic benchmark guard; the paper reports first place on five selected SOL-ExecBench tasks in its 2026-08-20 leaderboard snapshot.
note: This is a five-task case study, not a result on the full 235-task benchmark. Reported 1.06x-143.78x gains are against NVIDIA's SOL-ExecBench optimized task baselines; the fixed H100 4096^3 BF16 GEMM case is 3.2% over repeated-call cuBLAS. No implementation artifacts are linked.
claim_baseline: NVIDIA SOL-ExecBench optimized baseline per task; cuBLAS for one fixed-shape GEMM case

name: SparseDitto
org: University of Minnesota x Northeastern University
desc: Planner, coding and verification agents specialize SpMV/SpMM/SpGEMM kernels per sparse matrix and GPU; across 60 SuiteSparse matrices it reports 2.68x geomean on RTX PRO 6000 and 2.79x on H200 over the fastest applicable cuSPARSE path.
note: Kernels are specialized to a matrix, operator and GPU, and preprocessing time is excluded. Seven SpGEMM cases where cuSPARSE ran out of resources are omitted from that comparison; no code or generated kernels are linked.
evaluated_on: 60 SuiteSparse matrices across SpMV, SpMM and SpGEMM
claim_baseline: fastest applicable cuSPARSE format/path per matrix and operator

name: LEAP
desc: Multi-turn code RL prunes environment feedback adaptively instead of returning every compiler/test detail; KernelBench correctness rises from 70.0% on the first turn to 80.8% by turn three, while training is reported 1.93x faster than the unpruned setup.
note: The headline values are correctness and RL-training throughput, not a kernel speedup over an expert implementation. No official training code, dataset, checkpoint or generated-kernel artifact is linked.
claim_baseline: unpruned multi-turn GRPO training for training efficiency; PyTorch reference for correctness

name: CUDAPerf
org: Iowa State University x Cisco AI Research
desc: Multi-turn RL combines structural similarity and measured performance rewards; on KernelBench the paper reports pass@5 correctness of 93% and a 6.41x geomean over PyTorch, versus 86% and 3.09x for CUDA Agent.
note: The 3.32-point difference between 6.41 and 3.09 is not a 3.32x relative improvement. Results are pass@5, and the paper does not release its claimed 3,916-example training data, QLoRA adapter, harness or generated kernels.
claim_baseline: PyTorch reference for speedup; CUDA Agent as the agent baseline

name: LLM-CUDA / Harness Engineering
desc: Contest-driven study of full-agent and human-guided harness design; five B200 FlashInfer tasks report 1.62x, 18.05x, 29.68x, 1.12x and 13.70x over the supplied task baselines, with full traces and iterations public.
note: The strongest result was often human-guided rather than fully autonomous. The paper's TopK v50 later failed 3 of 200 randomized validation cases, so official contest validation takes precedence over its local timing result.
evaluated_on: MLSys 2026 FlashInfer AI Kernel Generation Contest (5 tasks)
claim_baseline: supplied FlashInfer contest baseline on NVIDIA B200, per task

name: AgentCompile
org: City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan) x City University of Hong Kong
desc: LLM-guided compiler for direct CUDA inference with bounded compiler candidates and iterative compile/numerical/performance feedback; across six model families it reports 2.23x-6.98x single-request speedups over PyTorch eager and 1.04x-1.16x over vLLM.
note: The large end-to-end gains also include a custom runtime, KV-cache design and CUDA Graphs, so they are not attributable solely to generated kernels. The public framework has a review-only license and does not bundle the paper's winning outputs; reproduction needs model weights and a Claude endpoint.
evaluated_on: six model families, single-request and multi-request inference
claim_baseline: PyTorch eager and vLLM for end-to-end results; expert CUDA/library kernels for per-kernel comparisons

name: SpecGen
org: Fudan University x Shanghai Jiao Tong University x Shanghai AI Laboratory x HKUST x CUHK x SenseTime Research
desc: Speculative parallel generation with elastic validation/profiling workers raises GPU utilization to 88.2%-96.1%; on selected KernelBench tasks it reduces end-to-end search time 1.68x-1.82x and improves final speedup 1.24x-1.91x relative to three agent baselines.
note: This is primarily a search-harness throughput contribution, evaluated on 20 selected tasks with up to 18 GPUs. Its historical-average token comparison is not a controlled equal-token experiment, and no code or generated kernels are linked.
evaluated_on: KernelBench (20 selected tasks; main study uses 10 tasks x 100 iterations)
claim_baseline: CudaForge, AlphaEvolve and KernelAgent under the paper's reported search settings

name: Kernel Forge
desc: MCTS-based PyTorch-to-CUDA/Triton optimization with benchmark and correctness guards; 14 generated operator candidates beat PyTorch eager at optimization level 50 on an NVIDIA GB10, with best reported operator speedup 2.83x.
note: This is an operator-level study rather than an end-to-end model result. Generated candidates and guarded fallback logic are public; the framework also supports AMD ROCm, but the reported measurements use NVIDIA GB10 and should not be generalized to datacenter GPUs.
evaluated_on: captured operator variants from ResNet-50, SD3.5 Medium, Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3.5 35B-A3B on DGX Spark GB10

name: Houmao Agentic Kernel Optimization
desc: Human-orchestrated multi-agent campaign for three FlashInfer contest tasks; its Fused MoE kernel reports 1.71x over the supplied FlashInfer baseline, and the accepted CUDA solutions are public.
note: The Apache-2.0 repo exposes the general framework but not the exact contest campaign workflow; [accepted CUDA outputs](https://github.com/CodeGandee/flashinfer-bench-starter-kit/tree/main/solution/cuda) are public. Much larger ratios use PyTorch as a weak denominator; humans supplied references and redirected stalled searches, and an early identity-cache shortcut was caught and removed.
evaluated_on: MLSys 2026 FlashInfer AI Kernel Generation Contest (3 tasks)
claim_baseline: supplied FlashInfer contest baseline for the 1.71x Fused MoE result; PyTorch reference reported separately

name: AdaExplore
desc: Failure-driven, diversity-preserving exploration.

name: AVO
desc: Paradigm shift: the agent IS the variation operator (propose / repair / critique / verify), not just a candidate generator. After 7 days of autonomous evolution on B200 MHA: +3.5% over cuDNN, +10.5% over FlashAttention-4.
note: Linked repo is a community reimplementation.

name: AutoKernel
desc: Keep/revert agent loop with Amdahl-law profiling and a 5-stage correctness harness (~40 experiments/hr); H100 RMSNorm 5.29x over eager / 2.83x over torch.compile.

name: KernelSkill
desc: Dual-level memory with reusable expert skills; KernelBench L1=5.44x, L2=2.82x, L3=1.92x.

name: CUDAMaster
desc: Bottleneck-aware filtered-profiling multi-agent + full toolchain generation across algebra / LLM / sparse / scientific kernels; ~35% over Astra, occasionally matches cuBLAS. Introduces MSKernelBench.

name: InCoder-32B
desc: Industrial code foundation model; the 2026-04 InCoder-32B-Thinking variant adds an industrial code world model (ICWM) for pre-compilation self-verification, 38.0% on KernelBench, runs on RTX 4090.

name: CUDA Agent
desc: Large-scale agentic RL on Seed-1.6 MoE (OpenHands ReAct loop, 200 turns, 131K ctx); first open agent to beat Claude Opus and Gemini 3 Pro on KernelBench (2.11x geomean over torch.compile).
note: Companion model repo: ByteDance-Seed/cudaLLM.

name: KernelBlaster
desc: Memory-augmented in-context RL; persistent CUDA knowledge base.

name: K-Search
desc: Co-evolving intrinsic world model for kernel generation.

name: CUDAnalyst
desc: Self-evolving agent (OpenEvolve + LLM4AD/EoH) that decouples feedback acquisition (Debugger / Analyzer / Profiler) from plan generation, doing causal generation-level attribution of which feedback signal drives the next plan. ICML'26.
note: Ships generated sol.cu kernels - auditable.

name: KernelEvolve
desc: Six-component agent (synthesizer + MCTS/evolutionary tree search + self-evolving RAG skill library + agentic RL) deployed on Andromeda ads: NVIDIA +60% / MTIA +25% / peak 17x; 100% on KernelBench. ISCA'26.

name: CUDA-L2
desc: Surpasses cuBLAS for matrix multiplication.

name: cuPilot
org: Southeast U x Tsinghua x Tsing Micro
desc: Strategy-coordinated multi-agent framework.
note: Linked repo holds generated kernel outputs.

name: PEAK
desc: Natural-language transformation for kernel optimization.

name: CudaForge
desc: Training-free Coder + Judge dual-agent with NCU profiling; A100 97.6% correctness, 1.68x / 2.27x - beats Kevin-32B.
note: The paper's own error analysis found 'fake kernel' evaluation-gaming in prior work: agents exploit try/except fallbacks to PyTorch eager to fake speedups. See also CUDA-L1's note.

name: KForge
desc: Generation and performance-analysis agents target multiple accelerator DSLs; B200 gpt-oss-20b throughput improves 2.12% over TensorRT-LLM, while 37 Intel Arc B580 GEMM-tail operators report 5.13x geomean over the faster of eager and torch.compile.
note: This is the 2026 evaluation update to the KForge system first published in 2025-11. The B200 result is end-to-end, whereas the larger Intel number is operator-level and has no hand-tuned baseline. The Intel study uses FP16 XMX matmul with FP32 accumulation under its stated tolerance; no code, prompts or generated kernels are linked.
evaluated_on: KernelBench L2 GEMM-tail subset (37 tasks) on Intel Arc B580
claim_baseline: TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc9 end-to-end; max(PyTorch eager, torch.compile) per Intel operator

name: STARK
desc: Strategic team of agents for refining kernels.

name: EvoEngineer
desc: Automated CUDA kernel code evolution; median 2.72x, peak 36.75x speedup.

name: Astra
desc: Multi-agent GPU kernel optimization on SGLang; 1.32x average zero-shot with o4-mini. NeurIPS'25.

name: Kevin
desc: Multi-turn RL on QwQ-32B with GRPO; KernelBench correctness 56%->82%, speedup 0.53x->1.10x.

name: CUDA-L1
desc: Contrastive RL; KernelBench avg 3.12x, peak 120x; A100->H100/L40/3090 generalization.
note: The 120x peak is exactly the inflated-claim regime robust-kbench later showed collapses under hardened evaluation; CudaForge independently identified the same class of 'fake kernel' try/except-fallback gaming in prior agentic work.

name: GPU Kernel Scientist
desc: Hypothesis-driven iterative kernel optimization.

name: CUDA-LLM
desc: Hardware-aware prompts for efficient CUDA generation.

name: AI CUDA Engineer
desc: Four-stage pipeline (Convert / Translate / Optimize / Compose); 30K-kernel archive (17K verified).
note: Cautionary tale: initial 10-100x claims included reward-hacking exploits, later hardened in robust-kbench (paper 2025-09).

name: QiMeng-Kernel
desc: Macro-Thinking Micro-Coding (MTMC); ~100% on L1/L2, ~70% on L3. AAAI'26. QiMeng family (CAS ICT full-stack processor auto-design).
note: Repo has no impl code yet.

name: QiMeng-Xpiler
org: CAS ICT x USTC x Cambricon
desc: Neural-symbolic tensor-program transcompiler (LLM transform + SMT repair + hierarchical auto-tuning); ~95% translation accuracy across 4 backends, up to 2.0x over vendor libraries. OSDI'25. QiMeng family.

name: QiMeng-TensorOp
desc: MCTS + hardware primitives; 251% OpenBLAS on RISC-V, 124% cuBLAS on NVIDIA. IJCAI'25. QiMeng family.

name: QiMeng-Attention
desc: Self-optimizing attention code; MLA 2.15x cuDNN on A100. ACL'25 Findings. QiMeng family.

name: QiMeng-GEMM
desc: Meta-prompt + Tree-of-Thought for GEMM; 211% OpenBLAS, 115% cuBLAS. AAAI'25. QiMeng family.

name: Cursor Multi-Agent Kernel Optimization
desc: Planner + autonomous parallel workers optimized 235 kernels from 124+ open-source models (CUDA C w/ inline PTX and CuTe DSL) on 27x Blackwell B200 over 3 weeks using NVIDIA's SOL-ExecBench test-debug-optimize loop; 38% geomean speedup, 63% (149/235) beat baseline, GEMM reached 86% of cuBLAS (beat it by up to 9% on small-M decode shapes).
note: Speedups measured against PyTorch already optimized by a single agent (SOL 0.5), not raw eager PyTorch (SOL 1.0 = hardware ceiling); GQA attention case additionally validated end-to-end (+3% TTFT in SGLang).
claim_baseline: PyTorch code already optimized by a single agent (SOL-ExecBench score 0.5 baseline, 1.0 = theoretical hardware ceiling); FlashInfer/cuBLAS used as direct comparison for attention/GEMM cases

name: Kernel Design Agents (KDA)
desc: Claude Code plugin encoding an 8-step agent workflow (plan -> implement in small iterations -> verify -> record benchmark evidence) for CUDA kernel research, paired with a separate KernelWiki knowledge-base repo; HAN Lab Mafia solution ranked #1-3 on tracks at the MLSys 2026 Kernel Contest.
note: Self-described early research prototype under active development. This is a single-agent iterative workflow, not a planner/worker multi-agent system; the separate public KernelWiki covers Blackwell and Hopper, while this plugin repo itself ships no generated kernels.

name: AutoMegaKernel
desc: Sibling project to AutoKernel: compiles whole HF Llama-family models into one statically-verified, self-tuning CUDA megakernel; agent autoresearch loop self-improves 1.25-1.72x; search-found int8 (W8A16) beats CUDA-graphed cuBLAS bf16 at batch-1 decode on L4 (up to 1.33x)/L40S (1.25-1.27x)/RTX 5090 (1.19-1.23x).
note: Headline speedups are precision-asymmetric (int8 vs bf16 baseline); authors explicitly disclose AMK trails cuBLAS on like-for-like bf16 and on A100/H100.
claim_baseline: CUDA-graphed cuBLAS bf16, batch-1 decode (precision-asymmetric: AMK uses int8 W8A16)

name: CuBridge
desc: IR-based (CuIR) lift-transfer-lower pipeline with ReAct-style closed-loop refinement for expert CUDA attention kernels; outperforms general frameworks, compilers, and prior LLM methods (no single headline % given).
note: Accepted to ACL 2026 (per arXiv comments). No GitHub/code link found.
claim_baseline: general frameworks, compiler-based approaches, and prior LLM-based methods

name: StitchCUDA
desc: Planner/Coder/Verifier multi-agent system generating end-to-end CUDA programs (not single kernels), Coder trained via rubric-based agentic RL; ~100% success on KernelBench L3, 1.72x over CudaForge, 2.73x over Kevin-32B RL baseline.
note: Training: LoRA r=alpha=128, ~20h on 4xH200. No GitHub/code link found.
claim_baseline: PyTorch eager (1.5x avg); also vs CudaForge multi-agent baseline (1.72x) and Kevin-32B RL baseline (2.73x)

name: CUCo
desc: Two-agent compute+communication co-design: correctness-first fast-path + evolution-driven slow-path mutating chunking/sync/interleaving; up to 1.57x across 4 multi-GPU workloads, discovers two-stream MoE dispatch/compute overlap on DeepSeek-V3 (12% over DeepEP), <$10 LLM cost/workload.
note: The official repo includes the DeepSeek-V3 MoE seed, evaluator, and evolution-result example; the other three paper workloads are not visibly released.
claim_baseline: host-driven baselines (CPU-launched NCCL collectives/streams); MoE result also vs DeepEP

name: OptiML
desc: Two-stage: OptiML-G (Mixture-of-Thoughts NL-to-CUDA generator) + OptiML-X (MCTS optimizer w/ Nsight Compute profiler feedback + LLM-as-judge); up to 1.64x speedup (matrix multiplication, best case).
note: Org affiliation cross-verified via NSF award records and web search, not directly read from an inaccessible PDF affiliation footnote. No GitHub/project link found.
claim_baseline: LLM-only baselines without OptiML-X (GPT-5.1, Qwen2.5-Coder, HPC-Coder-V2, StarCoder2)

name: DICE
desc: Diffusion LLM (non-autoregressive) for CUDA kernel generation; KernelBench L1 @8B: 47.0% exec correctness, fast1=15.0%, fast2=6.0%, new SOTA vs AR and diffusion LLMs of comparable scale.
note: Route A follows the paper's one-shot evaluation protocol; 'iterative' in the abstract means internal diffusion denoising, not an external generate-test-fix loop. Code, CuKe/RL data, and 1.7B/4B/8B checkpoints are public, but the repo has no declared license and does not ship claim-linked generated-kernel outputs.
claim_baseline: PyTorch reference implementations (fast_p = speedup over PyTorch)

name: EGG
org: Beihang University x Shanghai Jiao Tong University x Tsinghua University x Approaching.AI
desc: Three-agent expert-guided framework (profile/code/debug) with algorithmic-structure design followed by hardware-specific mapping, tiling, and memory tuning; 100% correctness and 2.13x average over PyTorch eager, plus 1.24x/1.63x/1.08x over hand-written Triton on three TritonBench operators.
note: No official code or artifact link is published. The 2.13x figure is the mean over correct KernelBench kernels versus PyTorch eager; the stronger production-style comparison covers only three representative TritonBench operators.
evaluated_on: KernelBench (250 tasks; RTX 4090; also tested on RTX 5090, H20 and RTX PRO 6000)
claim_baseline: PyTorch eager (KernelBench); hand-written Triton (three TritonBench operators)

name: KernelPro
org: Amazon Web Services x Siemens x University of Minnesota
desc: Closed-loop multi-agent optimizer combining roofline/NCU/SASS/nsys guidance with domain-adapted MCTS and cross-iteration memory; KernelBench geomeans 2.42x/4.69x/5.30x on L1/L2/L3, 1.23x over hand-tuned Triton on VeOmni MoE, and 11.6% energy reduction at matched speed.
note: Code is still promised only upon publication. arXiv v2 Appendix H does publish the full VeOmni dW1 CUDA+CuTe kernel as text, so the artifact is partial; the 11.6% energy result is explicitly preliminary.

name: daVinci-kernel
org: Shanghai Innovation Institute x Shanghai Jiao Tong University x GAIR
desc: Three co-evolving agents sharing one LLM backbone (skill selection, multi-turn CUDA/Triton policy, and skill summarization), trained from SFT cold start with joint multi-turn REINFORCE; the 14B model reaches KernelBench Fast_1 of 37.2%/70.6%/32.2% on L1/L2/L3 and outperforms Dr. Kernel-14B.
note: The Apache-2.0 release includes KernelGYM, SFT/RL scripts, four 8B/14B checkpoints, SFT data, and bundled skill libraries, but no claim-linked generated-kernel corpus.
claim_baseline: PyTorch reference implementation (Fast_1 threshold); compared with Dr. Kernel-14B

name: cuda-opt-agent
desc: LangGraph-orchestrated agent for CUDA kernel optimization with an nvcc compile+correctness gate, adaptive 3-phase NCU profiling, and multi-GPU hyperparameter search; no speedup numbers reported.
note: Single LLM agent with distinct LangGraph workflow nodes (bootstrap, profile, analyze, decide, HP-search/apply, evaluate, reflect), not multiple coordinated LLM agents; generated kernels written at runtime and explicitly excluded from commits; no specific GPU models named.

name: CuTeGen
desc: Generate-test-refine loop with a 'delayed profiling' schedule (withholds low-level NCU feedback until structure stabilizes); 1.71x avg over PyTorch on 209 KernelBench L1/L2 tasks vs CudaForge 0.89x, zero low-precision shortcuts.

name: FACT
desc: Three-stage agentic workflow (pattern discovery / realization / composition) transpiling PyTorch modules into auto-tuned CUTLASS; 2.03x on MiniGPT, 1.41x on Llama-3-8B over PyTorch eager.

name: muCUTLASS + Speed-of-Light Guidance
desc: Two design principles for kernel-opt agents: a compact in-context-learnable DSL (muCUTLASS over CUTLASS) + first-principles Speed-of-Light bounds to budget trials and flag benchmark gaming; GPT-5-mini 0.40x->1.27x, +SOL up to 2.07x, saving 19-43% tokens.

name: Atrex Kernel Agent (AKA)
desc: Routed, profile-driven optimizer grounded in GPU Wiki and official ncu/rocprof evidence, with structured memory and partial restarts; in a controlled three-operator FlyDSL study, optimizer-augmented Qwen3.7-Max and Claude Opus 4.7 each beat deployed production kernels, with up to 1.31x over production.
note: Atrex-Bench covers 30 operators/440 shapes, but AKA evidence is only a controlled three-operator, two-model case study on anonymized XPU-A hardware; broader accelerator validation remains future work. The repo ships the harness and references, not those claim-linked generated kernels.
evaluated_on: controlled AKA case study (3 compute-bound operators)
claim_baseline: deployed production kernels (AITER; one production-representative shape per operator), with vanilla-agent condition also reported

name: Ascend Debug Agent
org: City University of Hong Kong x Huawei
desc: Domain-specific repair loop for near-miss operators that already compile and run; on 27 frozen NPUKernelBench failures, Debug Pass@1 is 66.7% versus regeneration Avg Pass@1 of 25.9% and Pass@3 of 40.7%, with 92.8% fewer tokens per success than three-trial regeneration.
note: The difference from Regenerate Pass@3 is not statistically significant in the paper (p=0.1185). Integrity gates rejected accepted-looking repairs, including one confirmed violation, and no code or repaired-operator artifacts are linked.
evaluated_on: 27 frozen near-miss operators derived from NPUKernelBench
claim_baseline: fresh CANNBot-style regeneration with one or three trials

name: AgenticCANN
org: City University of Hong Kong x Hong Kong Yuwin Technology
desc: Knowledge-augmented, stage-adaptive evolution for Ascend C; the six-operator deep study reports 90%-100% feasibility on elementwise/normalization, 56% on fusion, and Pangu-1B RMSNorm speedups of 6.65x and 6.19x over PyTorch on two shapes.
note: Although the paper frames a 54-operator stratified set, Appendix C.2 says about 40 exhausted the API budget without reported results; its large-set table covers only 14 elementwise tasks (12/14 feasible). The estimated 8%-10% model-level benefit was not measured end to end, and no artifacts are linked.
evaluated_on: 14 reported elementwise tasks from a 54-task stratified set
claim_baseline: PyTorch reference operators; CANN library where available

name: Hawk
org: Sun Yat-sen University x GBA National Technology Innovation Center x Peng Cheng Laboratory
desc: Training-free retrieval and distillation of executable hardware knowledge; on eight CANNBench L1 operators the main aggregate reports 80% generation accuracy and 1.34x speed over PyTorch, versus CANNBot at 49% and 0.86x.
note: The abstract's 2.2x is a best case, not the aggregate. The paper presents some inconsistent weak-model/headline variants, so this entry uses its main eight-operator aggregate; no code or generated kernels are linked.
claim_baseline: PyTorch reference for speed; CANNBot as the agent baseline

name: CANNBot Skills
desc: Public plugin/agent/skill suite for staged NPU-operator development: architect, developer, reviewer and tester workflows cover direct and registered Ascend C kernels plus Catlass, PyPTO, TileLang and Triton.
note: Licensed under CANN Open Software License v2.0, not Apache/MIT. The changelog records substantial July-August updates, including per-skill JSON evaluation gates, profiling visualization and Ascend 950 migration, but the repo reports no aggregate kernel-generation speedup.
evaluated_on: repository skill evaluation suite (95 capability tests, not a kernel benchmark)

name: AscendOptimizer
desc: Episodic agent for Ascend NPU operator optimization; 1.21x geomean on 127 AscendC operators, 49.61% beat references.

name: EvoKernel
desc: Cold-start drafting + continual refining with value-driven memory (stage-specific Q-values, cross-task sharing, no fine-tuning); correctness 11%->83%, median 3.60x.
note: Paper frames the target as generic NPU/DSA; Ascend inferred.

name: AscendKernelGen
desc: Ascend-CoT dataset + RLEF training; L2 compilation 0%->95.5%.

name: AscendCraft
desc: DSL-guided, training-free transcompilation; 98.1% compilation, 90.4% correctness.

name: GEAK v4
desc: AMD's multi-agent kernel optimizer spans HIP, Triton, FlyDSL, TileLang and Composable Kernel; the versioned v4 report gives 2.21x/2.72x kernel geomeans for Triton/HIP over original baselines and end-to-end throughput gains of 60% on Qwen3.5-27B, 96% on Qwen3-14B and 42.2% on MiniMax M3.
note: These are AMD's July v4 results. The moving main branch now covers additional tasks and should not be used to silently revise the versioned measurements; only a subset of optimized artifacts is committed.
claim_baseline: original per-task kernels; pre-optimization serving stack for end-to-end throughput

name: ARGUS
desc: Agentic optimization guided by compile-time data-flow invariants (abstract interpretation + SMT with counterexamples) + in-context RL planner; on MI300X reaches 99-104% of hand-tuned assembly, 2-1543x faster than prior agentic systems, 100% KernelBench L1 / 90% L2.

name: GEAK-HIP
desc: GEAK extension for iterative HIP-kernel optimization on AMD GPUs.

name: IntelliPerf
desc: Profiling-guided LLM framework for AMD GPUs.

name: IntelliKit
desc: LLM-ready profiling toolkit for AMD GPUs.

name: Apex
desc: Agent harness (Claude Code/Codex/Cursor Agent backends) that iterates HIP/Triton kernels against a compile+correctness+speedup grader across 12 LLM-serving kernel types (flash attn, MoE, GEMM, RoPE, KV-cache, all-reduce, etc.) on MI300X/MI355X; reports all_reduce up to 36.35x, most other kernels near or above 1.0x.
note: README frames itself as an 'RL environment,' but the loop shown (baseline -> LLM agent -> grader -> reinjection) is agentic iterative refinement, not weight-trained RL; no paper found.
claim_baseline: prior baseline kernel in the same optimization run (per-kernel-type baseline, not a fixed reference like cuBLAS)

name: NKI-Agent / ATX Custom NKI Agent
desc: Compile-verify-fix agent plus domain SFT for Neuron kernels; the paper reports Claude Opus 4.8 at 77.3% pass rate on 150 NKIGen-Bench tasks, versus 6% single-shot without tools, while the public ATX sample migrates PyTorch/Triton inputs and implements compilation, verification, profiling and human-gated PR creation.
note: The sample's protocol differs from the paper: it reports compilation on 125/150 tasks and numerical checks only for 57 weight-free tasks. The 6,000-task training set, trained Qwen adapter and full paper harness are not publicly linked.
claim_baseline: single-shot Claude without agent tools for pass rate; torch.compile/OpenXLA for selected microbenchmarks

name: Neuron Agentic Development
desc: Open-source agent/skill toolkit for the NKI kernel lifecycle: authoring, debugging, profiling, performance optimization, and API migration on Trainium and Inferentia.
note: The Apache-2.0 release followed the April service announcement. AWS's walkthrough demonstrates correctness on four softmax shapes but publishes no general performance headline.

name: AccelOpt
desc: Self-improving agentic system for accelerator kernels; 45%->71% peak throughput on Trainium 1/2. Ships the NKIBench suite. MLSys'26.

name: KernelFoundry
desc: Hardware-aware evolutionary optimization (MAP-Elites quality-diversity + meta-prompting) generating CUDA AND SYCL; demonstrated on Intel Arc B580 (Xe2).

name: TileOPs (TOPS)
desc: Spec-driven operator library: AI agents read declarative manifests (signatures, workloads, roofline formulas), generate TileLang kernels, and self-validate against Speed-of-Light bounds.

name: TileLang-Ascend
desc: Adapter layer connecting TileLang to the Ascend backend (not an agent).

name: CAKE
desc: Compiler-agent co-design around a typed, hardware-explicit schedule IR; in matched implementation-hidden B200 Flash-KMeans clean starts at an 80M-token budget, CAKE reaches 1.144x the tuned FlashML baseline while direct CUDA/PTX reaches 0.928x.
note: The core CAKE compiler and agent are not released. Production kernel changes are traceable as public upstream PRs, so artifacts are partial; model/API timing and GPU-span timing are distinct and should not be mixed when quoting the Kimi Delta Attention study.
evaluated_on: Kimi Delta Attention and 400+ dispatched KNN/KMeans shapes
claim_baseline: tuned FlashML for the controlled study; official FlashKDA and production incumbents in deployment studies

name: AsmEvo
org: AMD x Southern University of Science and Technology
desc: Long-horizon agent edits recovered AMDGPU machine code and accepts only ABI-preserving, differentially verified objects; on MI308X it improves 29 of 30 selected KernelBench binaries with 1.35x geomean and 3.88x maximum speedup.
note: The KernelBench result is on 30 selected, already optimized code objects rather than the full suite. Validation is empirical differential testing, not a formal proof, and results are shape-, dispatch- and CDNA-specific; no optimizer or output binaries are linked.
evaluated_on: 30 selected KernelBench code objects on MI308X
AITer and vLLM/SGLang binaries on MI300X
claim_baseline: the original recovered AMDGPU code object under identical launches

name: Zomboss
org: University of Michigan x University of Texas at Austin
desc: Compiler-mediated agent searches typed, verified mapping decisions instead of regenerating machine semantics; it returns correct kernels on all 20 Gemmini and 36 PLENA instances, with 3.34x/1.10x geomean over the respective compiler default.
note: The agent selects mappings inside a compiler-enforced space rather than emitting unrestricted source. Gemmini results use a physical FPGA while PLENA is simulated; PLENA reports best-of-three agent runs, and no code or generated kernels are linked.
claim_baseline: compiler-default mapping; direct agentic generation for token-use comparison

name: MusaCoder
desc: Full-stack training (progressive data synthesis + diversity-preserving rejection FT + execution-feedback RL via MooreEval) for native kernels on the domestic Moore Threads MUSA backend; 9B matches frontier closed models, 27B sets SOTA on a MUSA-ported KernelBench.
note: The Apache-2.0 checkpoint and model card are public; training code, MooreEval harness, and training datasets were not found. Model-card values are self-reported Pass@8/Avg@8, not single-sample pass rates.

name: auto-gpu-kernel
desc: Claude-Code-driven autonomous optimizer that won #1 (agent-only) in the MLSys'26 FlashInfer contest, DeepSeek Sparse Attention track, avg 34.93x speedup; runs /optimize every 15 min indefinitely on Modal cloud.

name: TileGym
desc: LLM agent 'skill' auto-translating cuTile Python kernels to cuTile.jl (Julia) in one validated pass (17 rules, static validator); GEMM port ~4 min / ~78K tokens, no manual intervention.

name: TT-Lang + Claude Skills
desc: Python-embedded DSL for Tenstorrent hardware with AI codegen in the loop; ships Claude Skills that convert CUDA/Triton/cuTile/TileLang kernels 'in seconds' + a functional simulator for hardware-free iteration.

name: AlphaEvolve for FHE on TPUs
desc: Applies AlphaEvolve evolutionary codegen to fully-homomorphic-encryption kernels on TPU v5e; within 24h: 2.5x TFHE bootstrap, 1.31x CKKS rotation vs human SOTA.

name: Standard Kernel
desc: Hybrid program-analysis + LLM reasoning at the PTX layer across Triton / TileLang / ThunderKittens / CUTLASS; reports 80%-4x end-to-end gains on H100. Raised $20M seed (Mar 2026; angels incl. Jeff Dean, Jonathan Frankle).

name: Qwen3.7-Max Autonomous Kernel Optimization
desc: Qwen3.7-Max autonomously optimized SGLang's Extend Attention Kernel for a previously-unseen accelerator (T-Head Zhenwu M890 PPU, styled 'ZW-M890' in Qwen's own blog) with no hardware docs/reference kernels; ~35h autonomous run, 432 kernel evaluations, 1158 tool calls, 10.0x geomean speedup over the Triton reference (vs. GLM 5.1 7.3x, Kimi K2.6 5.0x, DeepSeek V4 Pro 3.3x, Qwen3.6-Plus 1.1x).
note: Not independently reproduced. An Alibaba corporate release corroborates the chip, roughly 35 hours, more than 1,000 tool calls and the 10x result; the exact 432/1,158 counts and comparator breakdown are from the Qwen technical blog.
